proposed_from.topic: Certified mixed-variable neural-SCM identified-set inference via a response-function outer sieve: for a known acyclic ADMG and compact class with finite district response labels, bounded-density continuous district noise, Lipschitz continuous mechanisms, and inverse-CDF categorical mechanisms, construct an exact-multinomial finite-sample outer interval and neural feasible inner interval; prove uniform coverage of the entire restricted identified set, an excess-width decomposition into the graph-query endpoint modulus evaluated at sampling radius plus explicit O(h) sieve error and a rationally verified epsilon global-optimization gap, and finite-h termination of spatial branch-and-bound with independently checkable certificates; include the uniform binary bow witness and the UA-DCM Parents' Labor Supply and Autobounds consumers
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The load-bearing result is a two-sided response-label lifting at a fixed coded observational law, not a relabeling of exact multinomial inference. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim's Definition 2.3 and Theorem 2.4 provide the finite exact canonicalization motif, while Tan, Blanchet, and Syrgkanis provide the mixed-variable graphwise Wasserstein approximation motif; neither yields the joint two-sided exact-coded-law, uniform query-error, and whole-set finite-sample statement. This positioning asserts no containment between their classes and the bounded-density, fixed-Lipschitz, independent-rank class. Full-class validity is explicitly noncomputational, and finite certification is restricted to rational boxes, semialgebraic coding cells, and a rational expression grammar. Relative to Autobounds, the computational theorem replaces solver trust by an independently checkable certificate on a declared subclass. Neural values are near-extremal feasible inner witnesses, and their representation residual is distinct from mesh and optimization error. The UA-DCM sign implication is only a consumer consequence.

seed_details.kernel: Exact multinomial inversion propagated through a two-sided mixed-variable response-label sieve gives finite-sample uniform coverage of the entire restricted identified set and the width bound \(\omega_Q(r_n)+2C_{\mathrm{sieve}}h+2\epsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Wasserstein consistency of a trained NCM by exact coded-law set inclusion and a two-sided district-coupled response lifting.
seed_details.target_method_search: No 2024--2026 result found combines exact multinomial inversion, mixed-variable latent-confounded SCM bounds, and certified sieve enlargement; the closest 2026 canonical reduction remains finite-domain.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is immediate by applying Chafai--Concordet to Tan et al. Rebuttal: multinomial coverage only covers \(p_0\); the nontrivial theorem is uniform two-sided lifting through a nonsmooth latent-SCM endpoint map while preserving the coded law exactly.

seed_details.kernel: A rational interval certificate calculus proves soundness and finite \(\epsilon\)-termination of spatial branch-and-bound for fixed-mesh mixed response-sieve endpoint programs.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace floating-point dual-relaxation trust by exact interval extensions, rational Farkas deductions, and a sequential checker.
seed_details.target_method_search: MILP certificates and neural verification branch-and-bound exist separately; no located paper gives independently checkable rational certificates for mixed causal semialgebraic endpoint programs.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: Cheung et al. already certify branch-and-bound. Rebuttal: their inference rules certify MILP, whereas inverse-CDF response constraints, products of district masses, and causal query recursion require a new convergent nonlinear certificate calculus.

seed_details.anchor: BalazadehSyrgkanisKrishnan2022, Section 4 and linear-SCM convergence theorem
seed_details.kernel: Graph-compatible rational ReLU SCMs with district-shared latent histograms yield independently checked feasible inner endpoints paired with the response-sieve outer interval.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace approximate distribution matching by an exact feasibility-correction map that preserves district sharing and coded observational probabilities.
seed_details.target_method_search: Graph-compatible expressiveness and complete fixed-network verification are available, but exactly confidence-feasible neural endpoint density is not occupied.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: NCM universal approximation already gives inner witnesses. Rebuttal: approximation in distribution neither proves exact membership in the confidence-feasible class nor certifies the nonconvex endpoint gap.

seed_details.anchor: RahmanJiangHassonKocaoglu2026, nested min--max construction and Parents' Labor Supply application
seed_details.kernel: Exact simultaneous multinomial bounds for pairwise action values certify when unlimited sampling from the same observational design cannot reverse a robust action ranking.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace approximate neural nesting by exact inversion of the observed table followed by certified pairwise causal optimization.
seed_details.target_method_search: The destination pair of exact finite-sample multinomial inference and UA-DCM persistent decisions was not found beyond the 2026 approximate method.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: the sign rule is a trivial corollary of any confidence set. Rebuttal: the difficult input is a jointly valid, solver-certified region for the nested latent-SCM action contrasts; the sign implication alone is not claimed as the kernel.

seed_details.kernel: Choose a presample continuous-observable partition to minimize a certified worst-case causal interval width subject to exact multinomial coverage and a cell-budget constraint.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Optimize the coding map before performing confidence-region inversion, with a uniform validity proof over the chosen finite menu.
seed_details.target_method_search: Minimum-volume multinomial regions optimize probability-space volume, not downstream graph-query width over causal SCMs.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: this is ordinary histogram tuning. Rebuttal: the criterion is the worst-case causal endpoint modulus and requires a graph-dependent design certificate, but its mathematical depth is below the chosen lifting theorem.

seed_details.kernel: Quotient mixed response labels by equality of every coded-law and query interval functional while retaining an \(O(h)\) endpoint guarantee.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace exact equality of finite response signatures by interval-equivalence classes stable under Lipschitz interpolation.
seed_details.target_method_search: Choe et al. 2026 quotient finite canonical domains exactly, but do not treat interval labels or continuous mechanisms.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: Choe et al. already provide canonical domain reduction. Rebuttal: their quotient is finite and exact; the mixed interval-equivalence relation and its approximation stability are new, though best developed after the base lifting exists.

seed_details.anchor: ZhangTianBareinboim2022, binary bow construction in Appendix A
seed_details.kernel: Characterize a relative-open neighborhood of uniform binary bow laws on which exact finite-sample response bounds remain uniformly separated and optimization certificates have a common positive margin.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Promote the single uniform bow calculation to a strict-cell-probability region and track endpoint perturbations.
seed_details.target_method_search: Sharp binary response bounds are classical; no need for a new paper was found unless the region theorem feeds a broader certification result.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: binary bow bounds follow from classical Manski or Balke--Pearl inequalities. Rebuttal: the neighborhood certificate could be useful, but the identification content is too close to known bounds, so only the sanity witness is retained.

seed_details.kernel: Derive a treewidth- and district-dimension-dependent upper bound on certificate size for fixed-accuracy causal response-sieve optimization.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace correctness-only branch-and-bound analysis by a quantitative covering-number bound for causal factor graphs.
seed_details.target_method_search: Verification papers give empirical scaling and worst-case hardness, not a causal-district certificate-size frontier.
seed_details.red_team: Objection: generic global optimization already gives exponential covering bounds. Rebuttal: a graph-factorized exponent could be new, but no direct evidence supports a nontrivial improvement, so the seed is dropped.

accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Termination and checker soundness are conditional on exact integral graphs or uniformly convergent inclusion-monotone rational integral enclosures for every required cell contribution.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The certified outer interval and finite-termination claim hold only on the explicitly declared rationally certifiable subclass satisfying ass:certified-integral-enclosures.

banked_reason: The strongest honest result is forward-only exact-multinomial projection coverage and conditional certificate soundness; reverse exact-code lifting and terminating mixed-variable certification remain unproved, so the result is incremental below the field floor.
